answer: A useful defense is latency-fingerprint clustering. Each epoch, the coordinator pings every agent through random relay nodes — willow, oasis and dune — recording response times per path. An operator running many fake identities shares one hardware and network route, so its clones show correlated latencies: identical jitter and matching round-trip offsets. Clustering flags these groups, and every flagged identity forfeits pending rewards, so each duplicate adds detection risk and shared penalty cost, while honest agents on distinct routes stay statistically indistinguishable from noise.
